title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space and defense sectors are buzzing with activity, from NASA's expanded contracts to SpaceX's latest Starship launch. Meanwhile, military satellite networks are getting a hefty budget boost, and the hypersonic test program continues to stumble.

themes.title: NASA Expands Contracts
themes.body: NASA's decision to add missions to SpaceX's commercial crew contract signals a growing reliance on private partnerships. This move could streamline operations but also raises questions about long-term sustainability.

themes.title: Military Satellite Spending Surge
themes.body: The Space Force's $437 million award to Viasat and SES highlights an increasing focus on military satellite networks. With an additional $1.4 billion earmarked for space resilience in the FY27 budget, the defense sector is clearly prioritizing space capabilities.

themes.title: Hypersonic Testing Woes
themes.body: The hypersonic glide-vehicle test has slipped yet again, marking the third consecutive quarter of delays. This trend raises concerns about the reliability of these advanced systems amid escalating global competition.

themes.title: Emerging Players in Space
themes.body: True Anomaly's recent $190 million Series C funding round underscores the growing interest in space startups. As the industry evolves, established players like SpaceX may soon face more competition from these agile newcomers.
